title: Who Certifies Effort? — Show Your Work: Understanding Time and Effort Reporting
display_label: Who Certifies Effort? — Show Your Work: Understanding Time and Effort Reporting
content:
Who Certifies Effort?

From the ORA eTraining module "Show Your Work: Understanding Time and Effort Reporting" (lesson 2 of 8).
Certification: What Does it Represent?
Effort certification confirms that salary charged to a sponsored project reasonably reflects the work performed. Because this is a formal attestation, effort must be certified by someone with direct knowledge of how that work was carried out. By certifying effort, the individual is confirming that: The reported effort is a reasonable estimate of work performed Salary charged to the project is appropriate and aligned with institutional policy All institutional activities are reflected within 100% total effort
Complete the content above before moving on.
Types of Certifiers
Primary Certifier
Primary Certifier: The individual The preferred and most direct method is for faculty and staff to certify their own effort whenever possible. The individual employee is best positioned to confirm: How their time was actually spent How effort was distributed across activities Faculty do not need to certify salary received from (1) their academic term contract or (2) summer session teaching contracts.
Alternate Certifier
Alternate Certifier: Knowledgeable Designee A designee may be assigned to certify project effort for employees only if they have first-hand knowledge of the individual's work. Typical Designees: (1) Project PI (2) Dean or Department Chair (3) Program Manager.
Knowledge Check
Knowledge check: Who is the most appropriate person to certify effort?
  - Payroll administrator  [incorrect]
  - Project PI  [incorrect]
  - Employee  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - HR representative  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: Try again.
  Note on "Payroll administrator": Correct! Great job.
  Note on "Project PI": We want to certify 100% of time spent on grants. If winter wasn't split between Fall and Spring we would certify for Winter.
